approval.cost: No listing fee or review fee is stated in the documentation read
approval.trigger: OAuth connection itself: no Square review or approval is documented as a gate. The 'Move OAuth from the Sandbox to Production' guide describes going live purely as developer tasks (production application ID, production HTTPS redirect URL, session=false, production base URL). Sandbox authorization works only with Sandbox test accounts and Sandbox credentials/URLs; it cannot touch real seller accounts, and no numeric user/install cap is stated for either environment. The optional Square App Marketplace listing does involve review: 'All apps will go through a QA process to ensure they meet technical and usability requirements ahead of launch. Should your app fail to meet our requirements, expect to spend some additional time rectifying any finds prior to getting approval to launch.' Developers self-onboard in the Developer Console, accept the terms, complete per-API technical-requirements checklists (for the OAuth API you must confirm tokens are AES-encrypted, the encryption key is not in source control, and the OAuth secret is not in source control), complete listing content, and submit.
approval.wait: Not stated (the FAQ says launch time 'can vary' based on application readiness, wireframe/QA testing, and content listing)

blockers.detail: 'Refresh tokens used with PKCE are single-use tokens and expire in 90 days'; the refresh response returns a new refresh token plus refresh_token_expires_at. If your app doesn't consume the new refresh token on each refresh, or lets 90 days lapse, the seller must re-authorize from scratch. The code flow instead returns the SAME refresh token on refresh.
blockers.howToClear: Persist the replacement refresh token on every refresh and never let a PKCE connection sit idle for 90 days.
blockers.title: PKCE refresh tokens are single-use and die in 90 days

blockers.detail: Different application IDs, secrets, redirect registrations, and base URLs (connect.squareupsandbox.com vs connect.squareup.com). Square calls out 'forgetting to change the base URL' as a common production error. The redirect endpoint must use HTTPS, must process the GET authorization response, and must securely store the tokens (and the code_verifier if using PKCE).
blockers.howToClear: Treat Sandbox and Production as separate applications in your configuration from day one.
blockers.title: Sandbox and Production are fully separate worlds

blockers.detail: If you omit scope, the default is MERCHANT_PROFILE_READ, PAYMENTS_READ, BANK_ACCOUNTS_READ, SETTLEMENTS_READ, broader than many apps need. Adding permissions later requires a NEW authorization request to the seller; you cannot widen a grant silently. (Conversely, you can mint reduced-scope or 24-hour tokens from an existing grant via ObtainToken with the scopes or short_lived fields.)
blockers.howToClear: Request the least-privilege scope set in the first authorization.
blockers.title: Default scope trap and no silent widening

alternatives: PKCE flow (public clients: mobile/desktop/single-page apps that cannot protect a secret; uses code_challenge/code_verifier instead of the secret; refresh tokens behave differently, see Blockers)
flavor.recommended: An application in the Square Developer Console using the OAuth code flow, requesting least-privilege scopes
flavor.why: Each application has separate credentials per environment: an Application ID (the OAuth client_id) and an Application Secret for Sandbox and for Production. 'Applications use the OAuth API to obtain access tokens that allow them to call Square APIs on behalf of Square sellers. Applications can request scoped permissions to limit their access to only the resources they need.' The seller authorizes on Square's hosted page and you exchange the returned code at ObtainToken for an access token + refresh token. Personal access tokens are explicitly not the pattern: 'Partner developers must not request nor use personal access tokens from the Square sellers who use their applications. Personal access tokens never expire and they have all permissions associated with the account owner.'

humanMust: Create a Square account and an application in the Developer Console
Register the redirect URL on the application's OAuth page and copy the Application ID and Application Secret per environment
(Optional) Self-onboard for the App Marketplace and complete the per-API requirements checklists
name: Square
nuances: Access tokens expire after 30 days; 'Square requires all partner applications to renew at a frequent interval' and 'recommends that your application automatically renew OAuth access tokens every 7 days or less', flagging tokens older than 8 days as a renewal-logic failure. Setting short_lived: true on ObtainToken produces a token that expires 24 hours after creation ('The lifespan of the short-lived access token cannot be customized'). Authorization codes expire 5 minutes after the authorization page generates them.

No implicit flow: 'you can omit response_type because only code is supported... The token response type isn't supported.' session=false is required in production so sellers with multiple accounts sign in to the correct one.

One-way revocation: sellers can disconnect your app from My Applications in the Square Dashboard, revoking ALL OAuth tokens for that seller; RevokeToken defaults to revoking the entire authorization unless you pass revoke_only_access_token: true. Square also offers an oauth.authorization.revoked webhook for real-time notice.

Square 'is transitioning to JWT (JSON Web Token) access tokens' (opt-in via use_jwt: true on ObtainToken); JWTs are 'significantly longer than traditional access tokens', so storage sized for legacy tokens can break.

Ongoing compliance duties are part of the product: your app must show accurate token status (valid/expired/revoked), let sellers revoke, encrypt tokens at rest (AES recommended), and never store tokens or the secret on a public client. Also note: you cannot later discover which permissions are attached to a code, so record the permissions you requested. Dynamic ports (PKCE only): mobile/desktop clients may register a redirect URL with a literal <port> placeholder and supply the real port at runtime.
prerequisites: A Square account and an application in the Developer Console
A redirect URL endpoint that uses HTTPS, processes the GET authorization response, and securely stores tokens
Token encryption at rest and a seller-facing token-status/revoke UI (Square requirements)

steps.detail: Developer Console > Applications > '+' tile > name the app. Pick the environment (Sandbox for testing, Production for live) at the top of the application page; each environment has its own Application ID/Secret and base URL.

steps.title: Create an application

steps.detail: Developer Console > OAuth > Redirect URL > Update > Confirm. Copy the Application ID and Application Secret from the same page.
steps.title: Register the redirect URL; copy credentials

steps.detail: connect.squareup.com/oauth2/authorize with client_id, scope (least-privilege, e.g. PAYMENTS_READ, PAYMENTS_WRITE, MERCHANT_PROFILE_READ, CUSTOMERS_READ), session=false (required in production), and state (CSRF token); PKCE adds code_challenge and redirect_uri. The seller signs in to Square and accepts or denies on Square's authorization page.
steps.title: Build the authorization URL; seller authorizes

steps.detail: On Allow, Square redirects with code, response_type=code, and state (verify state). On Deny you receive error=access_denied&error_description=user_denied and must show a user-friendly failure page. Exchange at POST connect.squareup.com/oauth2/token with client_id, client_secret (code flow only), code, grant_type=authorization_code. Response: access_token, token_type bearer, expires_at, merchant_id, refresh_token, short_lived. Codes expire in 5 minutes.
steps.title: Handle the callback; exchange the code

steps.detail: Encrypt tokens (AES recommended), record the permissions you requested, expose token status and a revoke path to the seller, and handle ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRED / ACCESS_TOKEN_REVOKED / UNAUTHORIZED errors. Refresh proactively via ObtainToken with grant_type=refresh_token every 7 days or less; access tokens expire after 30 days.

tagline: Self-serve OAuth with no review to connect sellers: 30-day access tokens, 5-minute codes, a strong renew-every-7-days expectation, and PKCE refresh tokens that are single-use and expire in 90 days. Only the optional App Marketplace listing adds a QA review.
